data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Evandor is derived from the name Evander, which means 'evan' (shining, light) and 'dor' (generation, people). The name represents someone who brings light and hope to their generation. The name Evandor carries the meaning “Evander's light, shining one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Evandor usually hope their child will grow to embody evander's light, shining one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Evandor
in_english.meaning: rock of the generation or a gift from God
in_english.long_meaning: Evandor is a name with its roots in Hebrew and Greek. The name is derived from the Hebrew words 'eben' meaning 'rock' and 'dor' meaning 'generation'. In the Bible, the name 'Eben-Ezer' means 'rock of help' (1 Samuel 7:12). The name Evandor can be interpreted as 'rock of the generation' or 'a gift from God'. In Christian tradition, the name Evandor signifies strength and stability, as a rock is a symbol of God's presence and protection. The name Evandor is also associated with the concept of a gift from God, which represents the blessings and graces that God bestows upon His people.

data.cultural_impact: The name Evandor stands out as powerfully symbolic of leadership and illumination. In ancient Roman mythology, Evander is known as a skillful hunter, shepherd, and founder of the city of Pallantium. Thus, bearers of this name are reminded of the responsibilities that come with leadership and the role they play in enlightening their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Evandor is a name that echoes biblical themes of light and hope in a dark world. In John 1:5, it is written, "And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it." The spiritual significance of Evandor, in part, lies in this reminder that even in times of darkness and uncertainty, we are called to shine our light for others, offering hope, guidance, and redemption. By bearing this beautiful name, we are constantly encouraged to live out this noble calling and radiate the love of Christ to all those around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Evandor may be derived from the Celtic words "evan" meaning "white" and "dor" meaning "door." In Christianity, this name could symbolize a guiding light or a door to spiritual growth and illumination. It may also represent one who brings enlightenment and purity to others.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval legend, Evandor was an ancient British king who converted to Christianity and is said to have founded the city of Eboracum (York) around AD 62. The name Evandor is derived from the Celtic words 'ab' (father) and 'andos' (brave).

Another reference suggests that Evandor was a legendary hero of the Britons, who according to a Welsh legend, was a warrior and a bishop during the Roman occupation of Britain. He is said to have lived around the 3rd century AD and is associated with the area of modern-day Gloucestershire, England.
